en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Noble Mother of the Constellations,
Spoken by the Buddha. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Scattered Official, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master for the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fǎtián, in accordance with the Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the great city of Aṇāvatapta.
At that time, there were countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
Accompanied by Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Saturn,
the Moon, the Sun, Rāhu, and Ketu—
thus surrounded and reverently attended by these twenty-seven luminaries.
This is the Great Vajra Samādhi Adorned Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, there was an assembly of countless thousands of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
whose names were Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and Vajrakrodha Bodhisattva.
Bodhisattva Vajrasena, Bodhisattva Vajrabhāṇī,
Bodhisattva Vajreśvara, Bodhisattva Vajravyūha,
Bodhisattva Vajraprabhā, and Bodhisattva Vajratala.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Universal Observer of the World,
the Bodhisattva Śrī, the Bodhisattva Padmadhvaja,
the Bodhisattva Padmagarbha, and the Bodhisattva Padmanetra.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta,
and other such great Bodhisattvas respectfully surrounded him. For them,
the Buddha preached the Dharma that is excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, and excellent in the end.
Its meaning is profound and far-reaching; its words are skillful and elegant.
It is pure and unadulterated, complete, immaculate, majestic, and as one desires.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi...
He immediately rose from his seat and, by means of his supernormal powers,
circumambulated the World-Honored One hundreds of thousands of times to the right.
He prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet and sat down cross-legged.
Beholding that great assembly with pure eyes,
he placed his vajra-pañjali at the center of his heart and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
There are various planetary deities whose physical forms are coarse and hideous;
their minds are frequently filled with anger, and they afflict and harm sentient beings,
either by severing their life-force or by wasting away their wealth and treasures.
They may diminish the spiritual vigor of people or shorten their lifespans;
thus they afflict and harm all sentient beings.
We only pray that the World-Honored One will preach the True Esoteric Dharma to provide protection for them.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!
You are able to compassionately pity and benefit all sentient beings by questioning the Tathāgata regarding the most supreme and secret Dharma."
Listen attentively now and reflect upon it well;
I shall explain for you the manner in which these various evil planets and lunar mansions [affect] Vajrapāṇi.
And to the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth,
one should offer the most excellent arghya water.
Together with music and other offerings,
perform each ritual offering according to the dharma to cause them to rejoice and eliminate all evils.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha emitted a great radiance from within his own heart,
named the Light of Compassion.
Entering the crown of all the lunar mansions and planets,
in an instant all the lunar mansions, planets, the sun, the moon, and so forth,
rose from their seats and prostrated themselves, touching their heads and faces to his feet.
Placing his right knee on the ground, he joined his palms in reverence and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha,
I pray that you will graciously accept me and preach the True Dharma for my sake."
If we hear that you protect sentient beings so that they may be free from calamity,
such that all fetters, swords, blades, and venomous insects shall not harm them,
we shall bind a boundary of the earth to provide protection.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata spoke this mantra for making offerings to the *nakṣatras* and *grahas*: Oṃ maṅkula-ya svāhā. Oṃ.
ŚVĀṂ ŚAVE SVĀHĀ | OṂ LOKADĀGOCUMĀRAYA SVĀHĀ | OṂ MṚDAYA MṚDAYA SVĀHĀ | OṂ PŪGA SAPA... [SVĀHĀ]
Dvaya-naya svāhā | Oṃ asura-satvāya svāhā | Oṃ kṛtsna-varaṇāya svāhā | Oṃ amṛta...
PRAJÑĀYA SVĀHĀ | OṂ KṢITI-GARBHE SVĀHĀ.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken these mantras, [remained silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Those who recite these mantras of the nine planets shall all attain accomplishment."
First, one must, according to the ritual rules,
smear a maṇḍala twelve finger-widths wide with scented water,
using either a vessel of gold, silver, copper, or earthenware.
Offer *argha* to the planetary deities while reciting the aforementioned mantra one hundred and eight times for each;
all that is sought shall be fully accomplished.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"I shall now further proclaim the dhāraṇī named 'Auspicious Radiance Mother.
It possesses the power of a great vidyā-mantra and is capable of providing protection."
All the lunar mansions and planets, upon hearing this, were filled with joy.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās who hear this sūtra and offer argha water as an offering within a maṇḍala, [they shall obtain great merit].
Recite this mantra seven times;
one will immediately attain wealth, nobility, and long life.
If one recites it daily, all malevolent planets and stars [shall be pacified].
It can fulfill all the wishes and intentions of sentient beings.
The *dhāraṇī* of the Mother of the Planets (*Nakṣatramātṛ*) is as follows: *Namaḥ ratnatrayāya, namo buddhāya*.
Namo vajradharāya | Namo padmadharāya | Namo sarvagrahāṇāṃ sarvasaṃpāraprakāśanānām | Namo nakṣatrarājānām ||
Namo nava-naśvara-śirṣebhyaḥ | tadyathā | oṃ mudite vārī vārī padme sara sara prasara prasara ||
Sara-samāra-samāra-tokṣṇaya-kṣiṇaya-mardanaya-gadaya gadaya sarva-vijñāna-kuru kuru cina cina pinā pinā.
Kṣāpaya kṣāpaya śānte śānte nande nande namaya namaya nṛtya nartiśaya tāmanna mamarkṣa rkṣa sarva.
*Sattva-śīla-sarvajña-tara-graha-he-bhīma-nirvāraya bhagavati mahā-maye prasādhaya sarva-pāpam* (Sattva-śīla-sarvajña-tara-graha-he-bhīma-nirvāraya bhagavati mahā-maye prasādhaya sarva-pāpam).
Pāṇi me sarvasattvānāṃ jañji jañji duru duru bhagavati jañji jañji sumu sumu jumu jumu bhava bhavai ugrī ugradate puraya mama mama.
*Sarvasattvānāṃ ca manorathasarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitasamaye svāhā | Oṃ svāhā hūṃ svāhā hrīḥ svāhā* |
Svāhā, Svāhā, Svāhā, Vajradhārāya svāhā, Padmadhārāya svāhā, Akṣite.
Oṃ vāse svāhā | sumaye svāhā | dharaṇi sustaye svāhā | mudaye svāhā | mṛtyuhare svāhā | sūkke svāhā | svasti kuru ||
Oṃ vāyasāya svāhā | kṛṣṇavaraṇāya svāhā | rāhave svāhā | ketave svāhā | buddhāya svāhā |
Namaḥ vajradhārāya svāhā | Namaḥ padmadharāya svāhā | Namaḥ kumārāya svāhā | Namaḥ kṣatrarājāya svāhā | Namaḥ sarva... [omitted] ...svāhā |
*Vamban svāhā. Oṃ sarvavidye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* At that time,
the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [proceeded].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This mantra is now the most supreme secret;
it can fulfill all the aspirations of sentient beings."
If there is someone who seeks long life and so forth,
they should begin on the seventh day of the eighth month and observe the fast and precepts until the night of the fourteenth day.
Having made offerings according to the Dharma to the lunar mansions and planets until the fifteenth day,
if one recites this dhāraṇī throughout a single day and night,
that person shall attain a long life lasting ninety-nine years.
All thunderbolts, dragons, ghosts, and malevolent planetary deities shall be unable to terrify them.
Furthermore, they shall attain the knowledge of past lives, and their aspirations shall be fulfilled as desired.
At that time, all the lunar mansions and planetary deities heard what the Buddha had spoken.
They praised him, saying, "Excellent, excellent! This is most rare.
We shall receive and uphold it," and they immediately prostrated themselves with their heads at the feet of the World-Honored One; then, they suddenly vanished.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Dhāraṇī of the Noble Mother Jyotirmātṛ.
